messages:
incident-bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT: SEV2 - /v1/generate 5xx rate spike + token latency cliff (started ~2026-06-12T02:05:00Z). Error rate: 8.7% -> 24.3% in 7m. Prefix cache hitrate dropped sharply. Paging @Eric (oncall) @Anya (sre) @Lin (ml-infra)
Eric (oncall): I'm up. checking svc-mux logs and prefix cache metrics now.
Anya (sre): seeing KV cache churn, prefix_cache_size doubled over 10m, eviction rate spiked. Also continuous-batcher queue depth increased. CPU on inference nodes normal but mem pressure high.
Lin (ml-infra): hmm we shipped tokenizer-v2 yesterday to improve tokenization stability. Could be key mismatch for prefix hashing. Any template rollout around that time? @Jess
Jess (eng-runtime): We rolled a small template change for chat templates at 01:58 UTC, but nothing that touches hashing logic. Tokenizer change is suspect. I can grep logs for promptkey mismatches.
Maya (customer-success): flagging CS — a couple enterprise customers reported failed requests and timeouts. They're seeing 502/503.
Eric (oncall): root cause hypothesis: tokenizer-v2 changed token boundaries -> prefix hash generation changed -> prefix cache misses + explosions of unique prefix keys -> KV store overloaded -> continuous-batcher backlog -> perf cliff. Steps: verify prompt->key mapping divergence, check prefix cache key cardinality.
Anya (sre): confirmed. I ran a quick diff between prompthashes for sample requests (pre-v2 vs post-v2). ~15% of previously identical templates now produce different prefix keys. That matches the hitrate drop.
Lin (ml-infra): exactly. More unique keys -> no effective prefix reuse -> KV entries blow up and TTL eviction churn. Continuous batching ends up sending many tiny batches -> throughput collapse.
Jess (eng-runtime): mitigation plan attempt 1: temporarily disable prefix caching for affected models to stop KV churn and let batching stabilize. Can deploy config change now.
Eric (oncall): do it. Roll a quick config flip to disable prefix_cache for the prod model family A (safe subset) while we do rollback of tokenizer.
Jess (eng-runtime): pushing config change: `PATCH /svc-configs/serve -d '{"models": {"family-A": {"prefix_cache.enabled": false}}}'`
incident-bot: DEPLOY: config change started by Jess (eng-runtime).
Anya (sre): monitoring: within 2min cache size growth stopped, eviction churn reduced, batching queue depth falling. Error rate trending down from 24% -> 9%.
Lin (ml-infra): next: revert tokenizer-v2 across inference fleets. That will restore stable hash mapping. Rolling back tokenizer packaging now.
Jess (eng-runtime): rollback command queued. Note: rollback needs model restart on some nodes. I'll do controlled canary then broad.
Eric (oncall): prioritize canary to two nodes in us-west1 then expand if green.
Jess (eng-runtime): canary completed, no regressions, expanding. Rollback finished across ~95% of serving nodes.
Anya (sre): post-rollback metrics: prefix cache hitrate recovering, KV store entries dropping back to baseline over 15m, error rate down to 1.2% now, token-latency normalized. Good.
Maya (customer-success): notifying the two affected customers with status update: mitigation in place, rollback done, we will follow up with root cause and timeline.
Lin (ml-infra): followups: create a compatibility test in CI that asserts stable prefix hashing across tokenizer versions, and add golden prompt set to detect drift.
Jess (eng-runtime): also adding a guard in runtime: if prefix cache insertion rate > 3x baseline for 5m, auto-disable prefix cache and trigger alert. Drafting PR: `runtime: add prefix-insert-rate guard`.
Eric (oncall): handoff: I'll keep monitoring for 30m. If stable, hand off to night oncall @Jess in next update. Current status: degraded -> mitigated.
Anya (sre): incident ticket created: INC-2026-3456. Impact summary: transient 5xx increase affecting subset of model-family A traffic for ~22m; customer-facing errors for two high-volume customers, mitigated by disabling prefix cache and rolling back tokenizer-v2.
Maya (customer-success): I'll follow up with customer remediation emails and offer 1:1 postmortem. Collecting request ids for CS by EOD.
Jess (eng-runtime): action items (assigned):
- Jess: PR for auto-disable guard + monitor alert thresholds. (`#1234`)
- Lin: CI test for tokenizer->prefix-hash stability + golden prompts. (`#1235`)
- Anya: runbook update: include quick config flip and rollback steps. (`#1236`)
- Eric: verify metric dashboards and update incident timeline. (`#1237`)
Anya (sre): adding note: avoid full immediate eviction TTL drops; prefer graceful TTL reduction and limit insertion rate in hot paths.
Eric (oncall): handoff to Jess (eng-runtime) at 2026-06-12T03:20:00Z for overnight monitoring. I'll update the incident doc with timestamps and screenshots.
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Assigned: Jess (eng-runtime). Incident channel will remain open for followups.
Jess (eng-runtime): ack. Will run through postmortem doc and schedule a blameless RCA meeting tomorrow. Thanks team. :party_parrot:
Maya (customer-success): customers updated. Closing loop after RCA. :thumbsup:
Anya (sre): logging final note: root cause = tokenizer-v2 introduced tokenization drift -> prefix hash mismatch -> cache cardinality explosion -> KV eviction churn -> batching/perf cliff. Remediations pushed and prioritized items tracked above.
